files.content:
import type * as React from "react" import { cn } from "@/lib/utils" import food from "./images/food.webp" import food11 from "./images/food11.webp" import food22 from "./images/food22.webp" import food33 from "./images/food33.webp" import food44 from "./images/food44.webp" import food55 from "./images/food55.webp" function assetSrc(asset: string | { src: string }) { return typeof asset === "string" ? asset : asset.src } const DEFAULT_POSTS = [ { id: 1, image: assetSrc(food22), date: "August 16, 2023", title: "The Future of Food and Tech", description: "Explore how robotics and AI are revolutionizing fast food.", href: "#", }, { id: 2, image: assetSrc(food11), date: "August 16, 2023", title: "Eating Clean, Feeling Great", description: "Healthy eating doesn’t have to be boring. Discover delicious meals that boost your mood.", href: "#", }, { id: 3, image: assetSrc(food), date: "August 16, 2023", title: "Pasta That Tells a Story", description: "Dive into the world of bold flavors and cultural traditions.", href: "#", }, { id: 4, image: assetSrc(food33), date: "June 10, 2023", title: "Food That Inspires", description: "Bright meals, bold ideas—see how vibrant food presentation can spark imagination and joy.", href: "#", }, { id: 5, image: assetSrc(food44), date: "April 20, 2023", title: "Energize Your Routine", description: "Power your day with nourishing bowls packed with flavor and crunch.", href: "#", }, { id: 6, image: assetSrc(food55), date: "August 16, 2023", title: "Sweet Trends to Watch", description: "From aesthetic plating to bite-sized delights, uncover what’s trending in the world of desserts and snacks.", href: "#", }, ] export type BlogPost = { id: number image: string date: string title: string description: string href: string } export default function Blog({ eyebrow = "Featured", title = "Latest Blog Posts", description = "Explore our latest articles, insights, and practical tips designed to help you stay updated, improve your workflow, and build better products with confidence.", posts = DEFAULT_POSTS, className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<"section"> & { eyebrow?: string title?: string description?: string posts?: BlogPost[] }) { return (

{eyebrow}

{title}

{description}

{posts.map((post) => (
{post.date}

{post.title}

{post.description}

))}
) }
